## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Quraysh and this passage. None is used in this draft.
- Wording a scholar should check first: 106:1 (the accustoming, and its grammatical link to the preceding passage as some read it), 106:2 (the journey of winter and summer), 106:3 (this House).
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Makkah, the Kaaba, the routes to the south and to the north, and the tribe's history; none is used.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. A reminder to Quraysh  (`#a-reminder-to-quraysh`)

Cited ayat: 106:1-4

> **106:1** بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ لِإِيلَٰفِ قُرَيْشٍ
>
> **106:2** إِۦلَٰفِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ ٱلشِّتَآءِ وَٱلصَّيْفِ
>
> **106:3** فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَيْتِ
>
> **106:4** ٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍۭ

### Claims

**c1** (106:1): The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh.

**c2** (106:2): It speaks of their accustomed journey of winter and summer.

**c3** (106:3): It tells them to worship the Lord of this House.

**c4** (106:4): It says that He is the One who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear.

### One-minute summary

The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh and of their journey of winter and summer [c1][c2]. It tells them to worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh [c1]. It speaks of their accustomed journey of winter and summer [c2]. It tells them to worship the Lord of this House [c3]. It says that He is the One who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear [c4].

### Deep study

- The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh (106:1) [c1].
- It speaks of their accustomed journey of winter and summer (106:2) [c2].
- It tells them to worship the Lord of this House (106:3) [c3].
- It says that He is the One who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear (106:4) [c4].

### Kids mode

The Quran reminds Quraysh of their journeys in winter and in summer [c2]. It tells them to worship the Lord of this House [c3]. He is the One who fed them and kept them safe from fear [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage ties the food and safety Quraysh enjoyed to a call to worship their Lord [c3][c4]. One reading is that the ayat ask the hearers to answer gifts with worship [c3][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the ayat do not say where Quraysh lived, who they were or how many; the draft names no place.
- Not established: which House is meant by this House, and which journeys are meant, are not stated beyond the words of the ayat.
- Not established: how the first ayah is joined to the rest (the grammar of the opening letter) is read in more than one way; the draft states the ayat in order.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the cities, the trade routes and the House that later accounts connect with the passage; none is used here.
